# Wharf 0.3.0 research

## Scope

Session 3 establishes durable state contracts only. Docker, agents, scheduling
policy, and report presentation remain out of scope
([`docs/wharf-sessions.md`](../../docs/wharf-sessions.md), lines 181-208).

## Evidence

- The state contract requires immutable run, trial, logical-attempt, and
  infrastructure-retry identifiers, append-only versioned events, materialized
  job/trial summaries, atomic mutable-state replacement, idempotent recovery,
  concurrent read-only status access, and versioned persisted schemas
  ([`docs/wharf.md`](../../docs/wharf.md), lines 223-236).
- The PRD intentionally leaves storage implementation unspecified as long as
  the state contract is satisfied
  ([`docs/wharf-prd.md`](../../docs/wharf-prd.md), lines 153-156).
- Session 2 currently has typed effective configuration and deterministic
  rendering, but no persistence or state namespace
  ([`src/wharf/Configuration/RunConfiguration.cs`](../../src/wharf/Configuration/RunConfiguration.cs)).
- The current solution has one executable and one test project; persistence
  should remain a reusable namespace in the executable rather than introduce a
  second application or infrastructure project
  ([`wharf.slnx`](../../wharf.slnx)).

## Contract to make concrete

The implementation needs a small public state API capable of:

1. creating a run with an immutable run identifier and schema-versioned
   effective configuration;
2. appending versioned events with immutable event identifiers and sequence
   numbers;
3. replaying events into materialized run and trial summaries;
4. applying the same event more than once without changing the result;
5. atomically replacing summaries after replay;
6. reading summaries while another operation appends events; and
7. rejecting malformed, truncated, or schema-incompatible persisted records
   without silently manufacturing success.

Logical attempt identifiers and infrastructure retry identifiers must remain
separate so retries do not create duplicate logical results.

## Recommended approach

Use a filesystem-backed store behind a Wharf-owned interface:

- one append-only JSONL event file per run;
- one versioned effective-configuration envelope per run;
- one materialized summary JSON file per run;
- atomic summary replacement through a temporary file followed by rename;
- immutable identifiers generated at creation time and persisted in every
  envelope;
- deterministic replay ordered by persisted sequence number;
- a per-run append lock for writers, with readers loading complete immutable
  lines and the last durable summary;
- schema-version validation at every persisted boundary.

This approach is intentionally local and dependency-free. It is suitable for
the current CLI, supports interruption tests using partial files, and leaves
room for a later storage adapter without coupling Session 3 to Docker or a
database.

## Risks and questions

- Concurrent readers must never observe a partially replaced summary.
- An interrupted append can leave a truncated final JSONL line; replay should
  reject or explicitly quarantine that line rather than silently accept it.
- Event identity and sequence idempotency need one precise duplicate rule.
- The event model must be broad enough for later lifecycle states without
  implementing later scheduling or execution behavior now.

## Explicitly not taking

- SQLite or another external database dependency.
- Docker, container state, agent execution, scheduling, resume orchestration,
  or report generation.
- A complete `wharf status` operator experience; only the reusable read model
  and read-only access contract are needed.
